It is very __hottest__ over here.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. hot .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective "hot" is in its positive degree, which is the correct form to use with the adverb "very."
 
• "Very hottest" is incorrect because "very" cannot be used with superlative adjectives.
 
• The correct phrase should be "It is very hot over here," using "hot" in its positive degree to be modified by "very."

Correct sentence: *It is very hot over here.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjective Forms:**

 
 
• Positive degree: hot.
 
• Comparative degree: hotter.
 
• Superlative degree: hottest.
 
 
 
• **Usage Notes:**
 
 
• "Very" is used with the positive degree of adjectives.
 
• Example: "It is very cold today." (correct usage with positive degree)

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

To __preparing the vine for plant__, it should be cut back to 2 ft.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **prepare the vine for planting**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The original sentence has a grammatical error in verb tense and usage. "To preparing" should be corrected to "To prepare".
 
• **"Prepare the vine for planting"** correctly expresses the action of getting the vine ready for planting.
 
• The phrase **"to prepare"** functions as an **infinitive verb form**, which is used to express purpose or intention.
 
• **"The vine" **is the direct object of the infinitive verb **"to prepare".** This construction correctly identifies what is being prepared.
 
• **"For planting"** is a **prepositional phrase** that modifies the infinitive verb **"to prepare"**. It specifies the purpose or destination of the preparation action.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is - **Option 4**.

The correct sentence is: *To **prepare the vine for planting**__, it should be cut back to 2 ft.*

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Ahuja is a __cleverest__ lawyer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the superlative form "**cleverest**" with the article "**a**".
 
• Superlative adjectives are used with the definite article "**the**."
 
• Using "**a cleverest**" is grammatically incorrect because it mixes an indefinite article with a superlative adjective.
 
• Since no comparison is being made among all lawyers, the correct form should simply be "**a clever lawyer**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1: clever**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Ahuja is a clever lawyer."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative degree** (e.g., cleverer/more clever) is used when comparing two entities.
 
• **Superlative degree** (e.g., cleverest/most clever) is used when comparing more than two entities and should be preceded by "**the**".
 
• When no comparison is involved, the **positive degree** ("clever") is used with the indefinite article "a."

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The speech you made today was __sillier__ and irrelevant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**silly**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The original sentence uses "sillier and irrelevant." The word "irrelevant" is in its positive (base) form.
 
• When two adjectives are joined by "and" and describe the same noun, they should generally be in the same degree of comparison.
 
• Since "irrelevant" is a positive adjective (not comparative or superlative), "sillier" (which is a comparative adjective) creates an imbalance.
 
• Therefore, "**silly**" (मूर्खतापूर्ण) is the correct positive degree adjective to match "irrelevant," making the sentence grammatically parallel and correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

Complete Sentence: *"The speech you made today was silly__ and irrelevant."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• **Option 1: "silliest"** – This is the superlative form, used for comparing three or more things. It would not match "irrelevant."
 
• **Option 3: "most silly"** – This is an alternative superlative form, also not matching "irrelevant."
 
• **Option 4: "more silly"** – This is an alternative comparative form, but it would still be a comparative, mismatching "irrelevant."

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.**

As she wants to lose weight, she __was started__ running.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has started'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option for the given blank is **'has started'.**
 
• Here,** 'has started' **that is **'present perfect tense'** should be used because **'the present perfect'** is often used for an action that started at some time in the **past** and is still continuing now. 
 
 
• *Example: He** has lived** in Canada for five years.*
 
 
 
• The **first clause** of the sentence is in the present tense hence in the later clause **the past tense** can't be used.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *As she wants to lose weight, she **has started** running.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

 
• दिए गए रिक्त स्थान के लिए सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प **'has started' **है।
 
• यहाँ, **'has started'** यानी **'present perfect tense' **का उपयोग किया जाना चाहिए क्योंकि **'presen perfect' **का प्रयोग अक्सर उस क्रिया के लिए किया जाता है जो अतीत में किसी समय शुरू हुई थी और अब भी जारी है।
 
 
• *Example: He **has lived **in Canada for five years.*
 
 
 
• वाक्य का पहला खंड** present tense **में है इसलिए बाद के खंड में **past tense** का उपयोग नहीं किया जा सकता है।
 
• अत: सही उत्तर** विकल्प 1 **है।

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The club __are organizing__ a two-day yoga and meditation camp for beginners.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'is organizing.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• 
 The error is **'are organizing.' **

 
 
• 
 Instead of '**Are**', '**Is**' should be used.
 
 
 
 
• 
 According to the rules of **Subject-verb Agreement**, If the subject is singular, the verb must be singular too. (विषय-क्रिया समझौते के नियमों के अनुसार, यदि विषय एकवचन है, तो क्रिया भी एकवचन होनी चाहिए।)

 
 
• 
 Therefore, 'The club' is a **noun phrase** that is singular. Therefore, 'Is' should be used.
 
 
 
 
• 
 The correct sentence is, *The club is organizing__ a two-day yoga and meditation camp for beginners.*
 
 
• 
 Hence, the correct option is **1**.
